newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo precious metals easier except for palladium.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo precious metals easier except for palladium.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo precious metal futures, except for palladium, were mostly easier on Wednesday, although bigger losses were pared as the dollar's rise against the yen gained momentum, traders said.
Palladium, which has been on an upward trend since December reflecting a continued delay in Japan-Russia export talks, ended firmer.
Gold prices ranged from six yen per gram lower to one yen up, with benchmark December ending down one yen at 1,347 yen.
Spot gold was quoted at $343.10/40 per ounce at the Tokyo close, against $344.00/50 in New York on Tuesday.

Activity in gold futures was lacklustre. In the gold futures market, private investors were slightly on the selling side, while short-covering by trade houses, reflecting the yen's further slip, gathered force later in the day, traders said.
The dollar surged to around 123.18 yen, a fresh four-year high in late Tokyo.
Traders said overall sentiment in the spot gold market remained bearish, but added the Fed's policy-making committee meeting, which ends on Wednesday, would provide some direction to the gold market.
Most palladium futures contacts hit record highs.

"Although gains were capped by private investors' profit-taking, physical buying remained strong," a trader said. "The tight situation in the Japanese palladium market is worsening as a buying rush ahead of the tax hike in April is expected," he said. Benchmark December is expected to rise to an all-time high of 500 yen, traders said.

Platinum futures tracked movements in the gold market. The benchmark December platinum contract was down four yen at 1,363 yen. Benchmark December silver was off 1.5 yen per 10 grams at 192.0 yen. --Tokyo Commodity Desk
